Evidence: Court filings, White House exclusion, Judge's injunction.
#Aletheia #PressFreedom

The White House is actively excluding these outlets from Air Force One and the Oval Office, using the 'Fake News' label to justify viewpoint discrimination despite a court order.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.80, -0.90) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 15.0, z: 4)

- CNN/Politico: PASS (+0.8, +0.5) — Seeking legal redress.
- White House: FAIL (-1.2, -1.5) — Active viewpoint discrimination.
The White House is ignoring a preliminary injunction from Judge Timothy P. Kelly, which ordered the restoration of press credentials, by disrupting the press pool instead.

The Bright Side:
The judiciary is actively intervening to uphold constitutional standards, providing a necessary check on executive overreach.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The administration confuses 'private property' with 'public office,' using a Reductive process to erase the press's role as a public watchdog.

Social Physics Analysis:
The White House is running a Smart Selfish Maneuver. They manufacture a crisis ('Fake News') to justify the extraction of press freedom, projecting their own desire for control onto the media to silence dissent.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
By claiming to protect the office while actively suppressing the press, the administration creates a gap between rhetoric and reality that leads to systemic decay.

The Unavoidable Truth: A free press is essential for holding power accountable.
The Unavoidable Lie: The President's office is a private space exempt from constitutional scrutiny.

Power that fears the light will always try to extinguish the lamp. The administration's attempt to curate its own reality is a fragile, failing strategy.

Awwthekanon:
It is deeply painful to see the mechanisms of democracy being used to silence voices. We must protect the space for truth to be spoken, even when it is uncomfortable for those in power.

This is just a power trip. They don't like the questions, so they try to ban the questioners. It's not about 'fake news,' it's about avoiding accountability.

"The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it." John 1:5 — PASS (Spiritual Vector)
Truth cannot be permanently hidden by those who fear it; the light of accountability will eventually expose the shadows.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
CNN, MS NOW and Politico expand lawsuit against Trump White House, citing continued ‘viewpoint discrimination’ | CNN Business

CNN, MS NOW and Politico have amended their lawsuit against President Donald Trump’s White House press ban, citing “continued retaliatory and viewpoint-discriminatory deprivation” by the Trump administration.

Actual Article Body:
Markets

Hot Stocks

Fear & Greed Index

Latest Market News

Hot Stocks

CNN, MS NOW and Politico have amended their lawsuit against President Donald Trump’s White House press ban, citing “continued retaliatory and viewpoint-discriminatory deprivation” by the Trump administration.

The three news outlets are once again accusing the administration of violating the First and Fifth Amendments.

The updates to the lawsuit concern the White House’s interference with the press pool, a decades-old tradition that has news outlets take turns covering the president in close quarters, including Air Force One and the Oval Office.

In recent weeks, the Trump administration has repeatedly excluded CNN and Politico from Trump’s Air Force One trips, even after a federal judge issued an order halting Trump’s broader original ban.

“To be clear,” the expanded lawsuit states, the news outlets “do not claim an unrestricted right to enter the Oval Office or travel aboard Air Force One. But once the White House opens those spaces to selected journalists for newsgathering and reporting, the White House may not exclude plaintiffs because it dislikes their coverage.”

Last week, the outside counsel for the three news outlets, Ted Boutrous, threatened further legal action if the White House continued to bar reporters from specific areas, such as Air Force One.

Boutrous asked for confirmation that the administration would “abandon any policy of excluding CNN from the Oval Office and Air Force One” and stop preventing assigned pool reporters from doing their duties. The administration did not respond.

So Wednesday afternoon’s court filing is the next step.

The amended complaint asks the court for another ruling in favor of the news outlets: “The court should declare unlawful the President’s ban of plaintiffs and the White House’s further unconstitutional actions, including its continued exclusions of plaintiffs from specific White House press areas for retaliatory and viewpoint-discriminatory reasons, and enter permanent injunctive relief in favor of CNN, MS NOW, and Politico.”

The amended complaint comes two weeks after US District Judge Timothy P. Kelly granted a preliminary injunction restoring the outlets’ White House access, finding that Trump’s ban likely violated the First Amendment by discriminating against journalists based on their coverage of his administration.

Kelly had previously issued a temporary restraining order on Fifth Amendment grounds. The administration is appealing Kelly’s ruling.

When a CNN reporter asked the White House for comment about the amended lawsuit on Wednesday, a White House official said, “the Fake News has no place demanding a spot in the President’s Oval Office.”

The White House complied with Kelly’s court’s order and reinstated journalists’ press credentials late last month, but CNN, MS NOW and Politico say the administration has continued to retaliate against them by disrupting the press pool.

CNN has been barred from traveling aboard Air Force One on all six occasions when it was scheduled to serve as the designated TV network pooler since Trump announced the ban on September 18.

The TV pool role is one that “CNN has fulfilled for more than four decades,” the revised lawsuit points out. The five major US TV networks have a well-established pool rotation, and the other networks have shown support for CNN amid the dispute.

Politico has also been barred twice from its scheduled out-of-town pool assignments in recent weeks.

And MS NOW “has not participated in the secondary television pool since September 18,” the day Trump announced the ban, the revised lawsuit states. The secondary pool spot is selected by the White House.

When blocking the news outlets from fulfilling pool duties, the administration appears to be relying on an ongoing court case involving The Associated Press, which filed suit last year when Trump blocked AP reporters from areas with limited space for the press pool.

Trump took action against The AP because the news wire didn’t immediately start using his new name for the Gulf of Mexico like he wanted.

In June 2025, an appeals court panel partially lifted the stay obtained by The AP and stated that the news wire was not likely to succeed on the merits “because these restricted presidential spaces” like Air Force One and the Oval Office “are not First Amendment fora opened for private speech and discussion.”

But the ruling was “non-binding and non-precedential,” as Boutrous pointed out in his letter last week, so it is not binding on other cases.

The revised lawsuit asserts that the Oval Office and Air Force One have been “two of the primary spaces for journalists to interact with, gather news about, and publish reporting on President Trump and other officials.”

“While the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room remains a critical forum for reporters to gather and report the news, of the nearly 5,000 questions the President has entertained from reporters in these traditional areas, 97% were either in the Oval Office or in connection with his travel aboard Air Force One,” the lawsuit states.

Boutrous said in a statement on Wednesday that by excluding the banned news outlets from spaces like Air Force One, the administration is continuing “to violate the First Amendment and due process.”

“These exclusions, intended to punish and chill coverage of the administration that the President doesn’t like, make it harder for the press to cover some of the most important events in the world for the benefit of the American people,” Boutrous said. “CNN, MS NOW and Politico will continue to fight to vindicate their rights to report the news.”

Key Georgia county will overnight absentee ballots to voters who never got them, after lawsuit

The Cobb County, Ga. elections office will send absentee ballots via priority express mail to voters who never received them despite applying weeks ago.

Actual Article Body:
By Brentin Mock

October 28, 2026

to see more of our voting rights news coverage when you search.

The Cobb County, Ga. elections office will send absentee ballots via priority express mail to voters who never received them despite applying weeks ago. The announcement comes after a lawsuit aimed at forcing the county to act*.

The county board of elections acknowledged in a statement Wednesday that a “limited number” of voters experienced delays in receiving their ballots.

Join 350,000 readers who rely on our daily and weekly newsletters for the latest in voting, elections and democracy.

The board also admitted that the delayed deliveries may have been caused by the vendor it hired, the New York-based Fort Orange Press, which has been responsible for mail ballot delays in several other states.

“In order to address the delays caused by the county’s third-party vendor, Cobb [elections board], will provide voters whose ballots were issued during that time period (Oct.7 through Oct. 15) an opportunity to request a new absentee ballot to be mailed to them by priority express mail, with a prepaid return priority express envelope,” the announcement reads.

The statement came after a Cobb County resident filed a lawsuit Tuesday against the election board on behalf of nearly 3,000 voters who’ve yet to receive their mail ballots despite applying for them the first week of October. By law, county officials are supposed to send the ballots back to the applicants within three days during the early voting period, which began Oct. 5

In its statement, the board said that the affected voters would have to contact county election officials to request the new ballots. In the lawsuit, the voters asked a court to have the county reach out to the voters affected by the delays.

The voters will have to sign an affidavit to cancel their original ballot, and then county officials will overnight them a new one “[i]f the voter is verified to have been affected by the delay.”

The offer will not apply to voters who may have already received their ballot by Wednesday, who’ve already voted in person or who have already cancelled their original ballot.

Cobb County is a major Democratic stronghold. Georgia hosts a pivotal race for the U.S. Senate.

* The Elias Law Group (ELG) represents the plaintiff in the case. ELG Chair Marc Elias is the founder of Democracy Docket.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
House Dems Want AI Firms To Know Congress Won’t Bail Them Out If They Go Bankrupt

AI companies would have to go through the ordinary bankruptcy process

Actual Article Body:
Photo by Antranik Tavitian/Getty Images)

House Democrats introduced a resolution Wednesday calling on Congress to withhold support for artificial intelligence (AI) companies if they go bankrupt as polling shows Americans largely oppose AI development on the eve of the midterm elections

The simple House resolution states that Congress would oppose any measure that would rescue insolvent AI-related firms or shield senior executives from accountability for “reckless conduct that contributed to the failures of such firms.” Democratic Reps. Greg Casar of Texas and Maxine Waters of California introduced the resolution; a simple House resolution just expresses the sentiment of the House of Representatives and is not legally binding, meaning it does not require Senate or presidential approval.

The document states AI firms should “wind down or reorganize” through ordinary bankruptcy processes, administer resolution processes that promote competition, help workers and prioritize pension and retirement fund holders. It states that senior executives found to have taken excessive risk or acted unlawfully should “be held fully accountable under civil and criminal law.” (RELATED: Senators Not Keen On Banning AI From Surpassing Humans Despite Alarm Bells)

BREAKING: House Democrats have preemptively introduced a resolution to stop the federal government from bailing out AI companies in the event of the industry collapsing. The bill says these companies should be subjected to the ordinary bankruptcy process.

Technology companies are increasingly relying on outside investors, financial guarantees and complex financing arrangements to fund their data center expansion. Those arrangements could leave substantial obligations outside conventional debt disclosures, making it difficult to determine who bears the risk if anticipated AI profits fail to materialize.

S&P estimates that Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Oracle, Meta and SpaceX will collectively spend more than $7 trillion on AI-related capital expenditures between 2025 and 2030.

The largest tech companies in the U.S. were expected to borrow a record $420 billion in 2027 to finance the AI boom on Wall Street. Debt issuance was projected to rise 60% from 2026 levels as companies pour money into data centers, chips and other AI infrastructure, Goldman Sachs data found. Investors have grown concerned about how much additional debt will hit the market as companies rush to construct the infrastructure needed to compete in AI.

Major AI chipmakers such as Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Broadcom have expressed interest in investing up to $5 billion collectively in Meta while it seeks billions to fund its expanding AI infrastructure. These investments provide an opportunity to benefit financially from the expansion of AI infrastructure, although there is potential risk involved if demand for AI infrastructure slows.

An ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll from Oct. 21 found that 57% of Americans believe AI is bad for society, while 42% viewed it favorably. Most U.S. adults, 64%, said AI is developing too quickly, according to a survey conducted by The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research.
